R433 — Source coverage and branch retirement candidates
Date: 2026-10-14
Read-only audit. No Git mutation, cleanup, build/test/GPU/process/environment inspection, private state JSON inspection, or benchmark/log inspection was performed.
Repository: /home/yayoi/ghq/github.com/yqYo1/Strata
Target current worktrees:
  bulk: feat/layer-major-bulk-upload-20261013 @ 85cb6b1968bd5c2156eed3b10dbb332f92ee95ac
  4K:   feat/layer-major-phase4k-20261013 @ 9c83ea6ba02a562d55cd90ae678aadebc2b88ae2
Both target worktrees reported clean. The repository has 81 local heads, 68 origin-tracking refs, and 80 registered worktrees at this snapshot. This is an inventory recommendation; it is not branch deletion authorization to this investigator.

Decision
Do not equate removing a branch name with removing code, or a history-only merge with product integration. The two target branch histories are separate from the old fork main (main at beddab2f, dated 2026-10-05); neither target is an ancestor of that old main. The target bulk and 4K branches, however, contain substantial shared prior Strata tuning/server history and most completed prototype commits. Before pruning refs, the proposed history-preserving target must make every needed commit/artifact reachable. Then choose source trees deliberately: a history-only merge preserves commits and evidence but does not select or install their code in the product.

The current bulk implementation supersedes the older per-expert-upload experiment implementations for the narrow Host-USM native-layout route; phase4k supersedes older scratch-alias, gated-region alias, phase-cycle/head-lease, and restore prototypes as the current 4K lifecycle implementation. The final implementations and their guards/fallbacks are represented in the target source; the older branches remain useful only as provenance while a consumer is still open. Do not preserve an entire old prototype checkout solely because its earlier code was different if the target source and required reports/receipts are already reachable.

Recommended minimum refs to retain until the named future work closes
- feat/layer-major-bulk-upload-20261013: current upload arm and the official bulk comparison in progress.
- feat/layer-major-phase4k-20261013: qualified 4K baseline and current phase/cache lifecycle comparator.
- One canonical full-context phase-probe ref: prefer feat/layer-major-phase-full-context-probe-20261013. It is the 8b48d17c tip; feat/layer-major-full-context-probe-20261013 is the same tip alias. Retain through the 262144-cell full-phase probe; remove the duplicate alias after the run is closed.
- diag-layer-route-union-census-20261013: keep through the planned union census execution/receipt. Its implementation is already represented in the 4K line, but it remains the named measurement worktree.
- diag/bounded-decode-route-ledger-20261013: keep through decode D-ledger consumption; the tip has one commit not reachable from either bulk or 4K target.
- diag/cpu-job-and-raw-bench-20261012: keep through the planned CPU timing work if Main will continue that diagnostic in this worktree. Its source/measurement history is already reachable from both target lines; once CPU timing is closed, its separate ref is not needed.
- feat/serve-first-row-adapter-20261013 (tip 88ebaae7): keep through first-row adapter work. This branch has seven commits not reachable from bulk or 4K; it contains implementation/review material absent from those target lines.
- feature/sycl: this is the user's currently open workspace branch at /home/yayoi/orca/workspaces/Strata/sycl. Do not delete this ref while the workspace remains on it.

The two aliases for full-context probe have identical tips and do not need separate refs. feat-full-main-context-probe-20261013 is an earlier 410904c9 source point and is already reachable in both bulk and 4K histories; it is not an independent keep candidate for the phase full-context task. feat/serve-first-row-logits-capture-20261013 at fd595aa7 is likewise reachable in both target histories; the later adapter branch is the distinct future consumer.

High-confidence retirement candidates after the listed measurements close and history is preserved
1. Completed phase/cache/upload implementation alternatives: feat/layer-major-phase-cycle-20261013, feat/restore-layer-major-prefill-20261013, feat-phase-native-head-lease-20261013, fix/phase-native-head-upload-owner-20261013, feat/prefill-scratch-lifetime-alias-20261013, feat/prefill-gated-region-alias-20261013, feat/phase-prefill-12k-20261013, feat/phase-cache-stock-bench-20261013, feat/phase-gated-quality-capture-20261013, feat/serve-first-row-logits-capture-20261013, and feat/fixed-history-logits-comparator-20261013. The active 4K/bulk branches carry the later lifecycle and comparison line; keep the standalone first-row adapter exception above. Retain the compact accepted reports and final receipts through reachable commits; duplicate raw measurement logs are not a reason to keep a branch.
2. Completed upstream/server update branches: sync/latest-updates-20261012, sync/upstream-v0143-replica-server-20261012, sync/upstream-v0143-server-lifecycle-20261012, sync/upstream-v0143-stream-recovery-20261012, sync/v0143-monitor-cache-20261012, sync/xe-v0143-nonfinite-20261012, sync/xe0142-v0143-functional-20261012, sync/upstream-v0.1.41-2026-10-09, sync/upstream-2026-10-05. Their server functionality is no longer an unmerged proposal in the active target history: v0.1.43 replica adaptation/CPU affinity, stream recovery, lifecycle/frontend, conversation-cache monitoring, and Xe nonfinite/functional updates appear as committed source histories feeding the current lines. Keep any unique regression/qualification report, not each staging ref. This is a source-history conclusion, not a claim that every upstream feature is enabled in every runtime path.
3. Closed source-only diagnostics and performance candidates with no named future consumer in Main's plan: the old diag/sycl-* branches (cache-route pairs, GDN-WY oracle, native dispatch histogram/role-plan/service-capacity, prefill phase/service-event qualification, static quota), diag/native-wrapper-parity(-baseline), diag/native-grouped-event, diag/repeat-capture-reader and fix/repeat-capture-reader, diag/prefill-leaf-service-events, diag/gprofng-native-smoke, diag/native-copy-queue-qualified, and diag/xe-host-issuer-ledger; and old perf/sycl-* branches (active-route grouping, decode-pool phase timing, GDN gate/factor/quad probes, IQ2S cohort/index probes, IQ4NL caller/event probes, streamed KV, native stream order, pool tasks, prefill copy/native-copy/stager-affinity/IQ4NL direct/async-boundary) plus perf/xe-prefill-emb-ple-alias-20261012. These are historical experiment branches, not required production paths on the requested follow-up list. Their source candidate reports/receipts remain the useful record. Do not discard a branch if a still-open NoNew/root measurement uniquely cites a fixture or input from it; check that consumer before worktree removal.
4. Older upstream benchmark and import staging refs: bench/upstream-v0.1.41-2026-10-09, sync staging refs above, and feature/sycl-upstream-faithful. Their value is provenance/fixtures; current server paths have later integrated commits. Retain the tested upstream baseline report and source commit ancestry, not necessarily each branch name.

Function-path coverage, as relevant to the pruning decision
- Layer-major bulk upload: current prefill uses optional owned layer-span eligibility and guarded private dense-cache layout; blocking checked layer copy precedes residency publication, while unsupported sources keep per-expert copies. R427's safety report identifies the exact source lifetime, geometry, fallback and retirement conditions. The bulk branch commit 85cb6b19 is the official current candidate; old layer copy prototypes do not add an independent future path.
- Phase/cache prefill: current phase4k tree contains guarded workspace admission, native-head lease, cache detach/refill and bounded lifecycle. The 4K report line and R431 source audit explain the current implementation. Earlier 12K, alias, phase-cycle and restore branches are implementation steps, not concurrent alternatives Main plans to run.
- Route union and decode D-ledger: route-union observation is at the common layer-major route-readback point before backend-specific execution diverges. Its logical-byte census does not change uploads or represent PCIe. D-ledger separately records actual route ownership/NT and logical extents, not time. They answer separate planned measurements; preserve those worktrees until each receipt is closed.
- CPU timing / CPU kernels: current source calls native GU, activation quantization and Down paths; R430 identifies where paired IQ3_S GU and Zen3 gather-vs-scalar A/B can be measured. Existing native batching and CPU-kernel branches are candidate/provenance work; no reported result proves an optimization win. Keep the CPU timing branch only for the currently planned CPU timing consumer; retire the other kernel/profiling probes absent a named follow-up.
- First-row adapter: the adapter branch has source/review commits not present in the bulk and phase4k trees, so it is a real separate consumer. The capture predecessor is already in their histories; keep adapter branch rather than both names.
- Server updates: the latest update/import branches are ancestral to both target branches. Their function and commit history are available through the target history if that is the chosen preservation target. Keeping old sync branch names is not required to make the current product source available.

Important cleanup gate
There are 80 registered worktrees. Only the two named target worktree statuses were checked here. Before removing any other worktree, Main must inspect its own status, untracked files, and active consumers; a clean branch tip does not prove its worktree has no local-only files. Several old branch-tip commits include retention-manifest/report commits, so preserving history must be confirmed before removing their only refs. Keep the verified compact reports/receipts and required fixtures; do not use branch retention to justify keeping duplicate traces, raw profiler timelines, or repeated polling logs. Preserve original test/benchmark status and follow docs/ARTIFACT_RETENTION.md.

Evidence reviewed
- Read-only refs, worktree registration, branch ancestry, target status, and source history summaries in the fork.
- Existing compact reports R411, R427, R430, R431, R432 and the named R433 user task scope.
- No private state JSON contents or benchmark result/log contents were opened.
